steps.goal: `supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql` is complete end to end: section (8) enables RLS on every public table, makes table privileges explicit (nothing for `anon`, column-level select on `persons`/`households`, no write privilege on RPC-only tables) and carries the full `ca_*` policy catalogue from DESIGN §6; section (9) revokes PUBLIC execute and grants exactly the 20 client RPCs (DESIGN's 17 plus `set_head_of_house`, `deactivate_account`, `restore_my_account` — orchestrator decisions 15/21) and the policy/view helpers to `authenticated` and the 10 `srv_*` RPCs (DESIGN's 7 plus `srv_load_unlocked_share_link`, `srv_archive_account`, `srv_restore_account`) to `service_role`; section (10) upserts the five private buckets with the `sermon-media` limit as one documented 50 MiB constant (Supabase Free) and adds the two `storage.objects` policies; section (11) holds the commented `super_admins` bootstrap. The SQL test harness exists (`supabase/tests/helpers.sql` with the `app_test` builders, session switchers and assertions; `scripts/db/test.sh` extended) and three structural tests — `01_tenancy` (cross-org isolation, anon denial, no 42P17), `08_rerunnable` (re-apply inside a transaction, identical object counts, every function definer + search_path) and `09_grants` (the grant matrix by `has_function_privilege`/`has_column_privilege`) — pass in the standing local sequence.

Step 1.3b: section (5c) with the 20 client RPCs and the 10 `srv_*` RPCs (DESIGN §4.4's 17 + 7 plus the orchestrator decision-15/21 additions named in Build item 3; `srv_claim_notifications` is `(org_id uuid, max_rows int)`, not DESIGN's `(int)`), the error catalogue (`raise exception using errcode = '<sqlstate>', message = '<snake_case_key>'`) and the status-string block for the two share-link RPCs. 1.3b listed every RPC with its parameter names in HANDOFF — that list, not DESIGN, is what section (9) grants. Read the section (5) convention comment (SQLSTATEs, the `app.trusted_rpc` / `app.cascade` flags, guards trusting a null `auth.uid()`) before writing the harness.

## Build
Work inside `9999_init.sql` sections (8)–(11), `supabase/tests/00_shim.sql` (one local-only tweak), `supabase/tests/helpers.sql`, `supabase/tests/rls/{01_tenancy,08_rerunnable,09_grants}.sql`, `scripts/db/test.sh`, plus the docs/handoff edits in Finish.

**Mandatory mid-step checkpoint (sizing):** this step holds two large bodies of work — the policy catalogue (sections 8–11) and the harness. As soon as sections (8)–(11) apply twice and `bash scripts/db/check-rerunnable.sh` passes (the psql counts in Verify are the only checks at that point; `test.sh` still reports no behavioural tests), commit and push `feat(db): RLS policy catalogue, grants and storage buckets (9999 sections 8–11)` BEFORE starting `helpers.sql`. If the session ends there, the repo is consistent and the next session resumes at item 6 of this list. The step's final commit uses the commit message in Finish.

1. **Section (8) RLS baseline** — copy the DESIGN §4.4 block: the `do $$` loop that runs `alter table public.%I enable row level security` for every table in `pg_tables where schemaname = 'public'` (NO `force`: the owner-bypass scheme requires it). Then make table privileges explicit instead of relying on Supabase's default privileges (the local shim has none): `grant select, insert, update, delete on all tables in schema public to authenticated; grant all on all tables in schema public to service_role; revoke all on all tables in schema public from anon; revoke all on all tables in schema private from anon, authenticated, service_role;` (add `revoke usage on schema private` here if section (1) lacks it). This positive grant block is an addition to DESIGN §4.4, which relies on Supabase's default privileges for `authenticated`/`service_role` (its section (1) only revokes the `anon` default): it is required by the local shim and harmless on Supabase — record it under HANDOFF "Deviations from plan" and note there that step 1.5 must put it in docs/MIGRATIONS.md as the rule "every new table created by a later migration (`9998_join_codes.sql` onward) needs its own grant line". Then the column-level block verbatim from DESIGN §4.4: `revoke all on public.persons, public.households from authenticated;` followed by `grant select (id, org_id, household_id, user_id, first_name, last_name, preferred_name, sex, household_role, congregation_status, directory_listed, photo_path, email, mobile_phone, work_phone, deceased_on, marital_status, birthdate_visibility, created_at, updated_at) on public.persons to authenticated;` and `grant select (id, org_id, name, address_line1, address_line2, city, region, postal_code, country, home_phone, photo_path, sort_key, created_at, updated_at) on public.households to authenticated;` (no `birthdate`, `member_since`, `youth_override`, `anniversary`, privacy flags, `privacy_confirmed_*`, `created_via`). Reconcile both column lists against the real `create table` statements in section (3) before pasting: the rule is DESIGN's intent (everything except the columns just listed), the names are section (3)'s — step 1.2b fixed the real column names (for example the phone columns) and a verbatim copy fails the paste if any differ. Then the RPC-only `revoke insert, update, delete … from authenticated` verbatim from DESIGN (persons, households, both leader-notes tables, org_memberships, org_membership_permissions, invitations, join_codes, join_requests, sermon_share_links, billing_customers, billing_subscriptions, stripe_events, notifications, notification_deliveries, audit_log, storage_deletions, account_deletion_requests, super_admins). Then lock the decision-15 archive columns: `revoke update on public.profiles from authenticated; grant update (display_name, last_org_id) on public.profiles to authenticated;` — `archived_at`, `archived_by` and `archive_reason` change only through `deactivate_account`, `request_account_deletion`, `restore_my_account`, `srv_archive_account` and `srv_restore_account` (definer RPCs); without this column list a user archived by an admin could clear `archived_at` with a plain `update` and defeat `restore_my_account`'s `account_archived_by_admin` rule (`email` is trigger-synced and needs no client update). DESIGN §6 says only "update = own row" for `profiles`; record the column list under Deviations. Re-issue `grant select on public.directory_households, public.directory_persons, public.org_directory_info to authenticated;` (views are owned by the migration owner, so they read the base tables with owner privileges; the functions they call — `app.household_view_level`, `app.is_adult`, `app.member_org_ids`, `app.fellowship_visible_org_ids` — are executed with the CALLER's privileges, which is why section (9) grants them to `authenticated`).
2. **Section (8) policy catalogue** — one `drop policy if exists <name> on <table>;` immediately before each `create policy`, names `ca_<table>_<op>_<who>`, every write policy also requires `app.org_writable(org_id)`, and viewer facts always in the InitPlan form `org_id = any((select app.member_org_ids()))` / `org_id = any((select app.perm_org_ids('<perm>')))` (never a correlated call per row). `service_role` gets no policies (BYPASSRLS). Implement DESIGN §6's table:
   - `organizations`: select `ca_orgs_select_fellowship` (verbatim from DESIGN: member or `app.fellowship_visible_org_ids()`); insert/update `ca_organizations_insert_super` / `ca_organizations_update_super` (`app.is_super_admin()`); no delete policy (`cancelled` + purge).
   - `organization_settings`: select member (`ca_organization_settings_select_member`); update `ca_organization_settings_update_org_settings` = `org.settings` ∧ writable; no insert/delete policy (the `on_org_created` trigger inserts as definer).
   - `fellowships` / `fellowship_memberships`: select when the caller is a member of a linked org (`exists (select 1 from public.fellowship_memberships fm where fm.fellowship_id = <id> and fm.org_id = any((select app.member_org_ids())))`) or super admin; insert/update/delete super only.
   - `profiles`: `ca_profiles_select_org_admin` verbatim from DESIGN (own row, or a `users.create`/`users.delete`/`users.edit_permissions` holder of a shared org); insert/update own row (`user_id = auth.uid()`; the update is additionally column-limited by item 1); no delete.
   - `super_admins`: select super only; no writes (bootstrap INSERT runs as `postgres`).
   - `org_memberships`, `org_membership_permissions`: select own row (`user_id = auth.uid()`, via the membership for the permissions table) or any `users.*` holder of the org; no write policies (RPC-only; the revoke above already removes the privilege — the absence of policies is the second lock).
   - `invitations`, `join_codes`: select `users.create`; `join_requests`: select `users.create` or own (`user_id = auth.uid()`); no write policies.
   - `households` / `persons`: `ca_households_select_visible` / `ca_persons_select_visible` = `exists (select 1 from public.directory_households d where d.id = households.id)` (DESIGN: "base table only through the view's rule"); no write policies. `household_leader_notes` / `person_leader_notes`: select `org_id = any((select app.directory_admin_org_ids()))`; no write policies.
   - `audience_groups`: select member; insert/update/delete `announcements.create` or `org.settings` ∧ writable, and delete additionally `kind = 'custom'` (system rows are never deleted; the 1.3a `guard_system_audience_groups` trigger is the second lock and raises `system_group_immutable` on a rename or delete of a system row). `audience_group_members`: select, insert, delete for the same manager pair only; no update policy.
   - `calendars`: select member ∧ `app.user_in_group(view_audience_group_id)`; insert/update/delete `org.settings` ∧ writable.
   - `events`: select member ∧ calendar visible (`exists (select 1 from public.calendars c where c.id = events.calendar_id)` — the calendar policy applies inside the subquery) ∧ (`status = 'approved'` ∨ `submitted_by = auth.uid()` ∨ `announcements.edit`); insert (`ca_events_insert`) member ∧ writable ∧ `submitted_by = auth.uid()` ∧ (`announcements.create` ∨ (`organization_settings.members_can_submit_events` ∧ the calendar's `calendars.members_can_submit` ∧ `app.user_in_group(<calendar's submit_audience_group_id>)`)) — DESIGN §6 lists only `members_can_submit_events`; the leader branch (`∨ announcements.create`, so managers are never blocked by either toggle) and the per-calendar `members_can_submit` column are orchestrator decision 21 / G12. The 1.3a `force_event_pending` trigger enforces the same closed-calendar rule and raises `calendar_submissions_closed` (42501) BEFORE the `with check` runs (Postgres evaluates RLS `with check` after `before row` triggers), so a member's insert on a closed calendar fails with that key while the policy remains the second lock; it also forces `pending`/`push = false` for non-creators when `events_require_approval` is on and stores `approved`/`push = false` when it is off. 1.4c tests all of it; record the reading under Deviations; update `using` own-while-pending or `announcements.edit`, `with check` the same plus `status = 'pending'` unless `announcements.edit`; delete `announcements.delete` or own pending.
   - `sermons`: `ca_sermons_select_members` and `ca_sermons_insert_by_kind` verbatim from DESIGN §4.4; `ca_sermons_update_by_kind` with the same media-kind split in both `using` and `with check`; `ca_sermons_delete_sermons_delete` = `sermons.delete` ∧ writable.
   - `sermon_share_links`: select `sermons.link` or `sermons.upload`; no write policies (RPC-only).
   - `announcements`: select member ∧ `publish_at <= now()` ∧ (`expires_at is null or expires_at > now()`) ∧ `app.user_in_group(audience_group_id)`, or any of `announcements.create/edit/delete`; insert `announcements.create`; update `announcements.edit`; delete `announcements.delete` — each ∧ writable.
   - `bulletins`: select member ∧ `publish_at <= now()`, or `bulletins.upload`; insert/update/delete `bulletins.upload` ∧ writable. `documents`: select member ∧ published ∧ `app.user_in_group(audience_group_id)`, or `documents.upload`; writes `documents.upload` ∧ writable.
   - `surveys`, `survey_questions`: select member ∧ `status = 'open'` ∧ inside `[opens_at, closes_at]` (nulls open-ended) ∧ `app.user_in_group(audience_group_id)`, or any of `announcements.create/edit/delete` (DESIGN §6 says `announcements.create` only; the three-key form follows the PLAN §4 / DESIGN §5 survey mapping `announcements.create/edit/delete` — record it under Deviations) (questions via `exists` on the parent survey); insert `announcements.create`; update `announcements.edit` (the 1.3a `freeze_survey_shape` trigger guards the shape); delete `announcements.delete`.
   - `survey_responses`: select own (`person_id = app.my_person_id(org_id)` or `household_id = any((select app.my_household_ids()))`) or the three announcement permissions; insert member ∧ writable ∧ survey open/in window/in audience (the `stamp_response_scope` trigger overwrites the scope columns); update own ∧ survey open ∧ `allow_edit` (per_household → any adult of the household through `my_household_ids`); no delete. `survey_answers`: select/insert/update through `exists` on the visible/own response with the same conditions; no delete.
   - `push_devices`, `notification_preferences`: one `for all` policy each, `using`/`with check` `user_id = auth.uid()` (preferences additionally `org_id = any((select app.member_org_ids()))` in `with check`).
   - `notifications`: `ca_notifications_select` = `org_id = any((select app.perm_org_ids('announcements.create'))) or org_id = any((select app.perm_org_ids('announcements.edit'))) or org_id = any((select app.perm_org_ids('announcements.delete'))) or (kind = 'bulletin' and org_id = any((select app.perm_org_ids('bulletins.upload'))))` — orchestrator decision 21 / G9: a `bulletins.upload`-only leader sees the outbox rows of bulletins (their own push status) and no announcement/event/survey rows; DESIGN §6 says `announcements.*` managers only, so record the bulletin branch under Deviations (1.4c asserts it; 3.5b/3.6a rely on it); no write policies (trigger-fed as definer, claimed by `service_role`). `notification_deliveries`, `stripe_events`, `storage_deletions`: select super admin only. `billing_customers`, `billing_subscriptions`: select `org.settings` or super. `audit_log`: select `org.settings` or super; no writes (trigger-fed as definer). `account_deletion_requests`: select own (`user_id = auth.uid()`; the row carries `scheduled_for`, decision 15); no client write policies — `request_account_deletion`, `restore_my_account` (definer RPCs) and the `srv_archive_account` / `srv_restore_account` / `srv_process_account_deletions` service RPCs are the only writers, and `service_role` bypasses RLS, so DESIGN's "update = service" needs no policy.
   Every public table ends up with at least one select policy.
3. **Section (9) grants** — copy the DESIGN §4.4 block verbatim: `revoke execute on all functions in schema public from public, anon, authenticated; revoke execute on all functions in schema app from public, anon, authenticated;` then the three `grant execute` statements: the `app.*` helper list to `authenticated` (add `app.can_read_object(text, text)` and `app.can_write_object(text, text)` because the storage policies call them as the querying role; add `app.person_in_group(uuid, uuid)` only if a policy references it directly), the 20 client RPCs to `authenticated` with the exact signatures 1.3b created — DESIGN §4.4's 17 (`my_context()`, `set_membership_permissions(uuid, public.permission_key[])`, `set_membership_status(uuid, public.membership_status)`, `remove_membership(uuid)`, `create_invitation(uuid, text, uuid, public.permission_key[])`, `revoke_invitation(uuid)`, `accept_invitation(text)`, `save_household(jsonb)`, `save_person(jsonb)`, `delete_person(uuid)`, `set_household_privacy(uuid, boolean, boolean, boolean)`, `save_leader_notes(text, uuid, text)`, `set_congregation_status(uuid, public.congregation_status, date)`, `create_share_link(uuid, text, text, timestamptz, int)`, `revoke_share_link(uuid)`, `submit_survey_response(uuid, jsonb)`, `request_account_deletion()`) plus the three of orchestrator decisions 15/21: `set_head_of_house(uuid, uuid, public.household_role)`, `deactivate_account()`, `restore_my_account()` — and the 10 `srv_*` RPCs to `service_role` only — DESIGN's 7 with `srv_claim_notifications` in its decision-21 form (`srv_resolve_share_link(bytea, text, text)`, `srv_audience_user_ids(uuid, uuid)`, `srv_enqueue_due_notifications()`, `srv_claim_notifications(uuid, int)`, `srv_attach_user(uuid, uuid, uuid, text, public.permission_key[])`, `srv_process_account_deletions()`, `srv_housekeeping()`) plus `srv_load_unlocked_share_link(uuid)`, `srv_archive_account(uuid, text)`, `srv_restore_account(uuid)`. Before writing the grants run `select proname, pg_get_function_identity_arguments(oid) from pg_proc where pronamespace = 'public'::regnamespace order by 1` and grant what exists (a grant on a non-existent signature fails the paste); any difference from the lists above goes to HANDOFF. `anon` receives nothing. Trigger functions, `app.require_*`, `app.rate_limit_hit` / `app.rate_limit_check`, `app.person_in_kind`, `app.archive_account`, `app.share_link_payload` and every `srv_*` stay unreachable for `authenticated`.
4. **Section (10) storage** — start with the single constant: a `do $$ declare c_sermon_media_limit bigint := 52428800; -- 50 MiB: Supabase FREE plan cap (founder decision 10). To raise it on Pro: raise the project's global upload limit in the dashboard, then ship a new migration (supabase/migrations/9995_storage_limit.sql) that repeats ONLY this bucket upsert for sermon-media with 2147483648 (2 GiB) — never edit this file once it is in the HANDOFF ledger. Keep NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB (docs/ENV.md) in sync. begin … end $$;` block that executes the `insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public, file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types) values … on conflict (id) do update set public = excluded.public, file_size_limit = excluded.file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types = excluded.allowed_mime_types` statement from DESIGN §4.4 with these rows: `sermon-media` (`c_sermon_media_limit`, MIME `audio/mpeg, audio/mp4, audio/aac, audio/ogg, audio/wav, audio/x-m4a, video/mp4, video/quicktime, video/webm`), `bulletins` (26214400; `application/pdf, image/jpeg, image/png`), `documents` (52428800; the DESIGN allow-list: pdf, jpeg, png, text/plain, msword, docx, xls, xlsx), `directory-photos` (10485760; jpeg, png, webp), `org-assets` (5242880; jpeg, png, webp — no SVG). All `public = false`. Then the two policies: `drop policy if exists ca_storage_select on storage.objects; create policy ca_storage_select on storage.objects for select to authenticated using (app.can_read_object(bucket_id, name));` and `ca_storage_insert … for insert to authenticated with check (app.can_write_object(bucket_id, name));` — NO update/delete policies for `authenticated` (DESIGN §6: deletions only via `storage_deletions` + service role). Do not `enable row level security` on `storage.objects` in the migration (Supabase already has it; `postgres` does not own the table) — the shim does it locally (item 6).
5. **Section (11) bootstrap** — the commented block from DESIGN §4.4 with a placeholder instead of any real address: `-- insert into public.super_admins (user_id) select id from auth.users where email = '<FOUNDER_EMAIL>' on conflict do nothing;` with comment lines: paste AFTER signing up once on the deployed site; replace `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>`; record the date in the HANDOFF ledger. No real email in the file.
6. **`supabase/tests/00_shim.sql`** (local-only) — verify, do not re-invent: step 1.2a (revised 2026-09-08, split 2026-09-15) already gives `service_role` BYPASSRLS (`login_service()` relies on it), enables RLS on `storage.objects`, grants Supabase's table privileges (`select, insert, update, delete` on `storage.objects` / `storage.buckets`) to `authenticated` and `service_role` (without them 1.4c's storage tests would fail with 42501 before any policy is exercised — the `ca_storage_*` policies and the ABSENCE of update/delete policies are what filter), and `scripts/db/local-up.sh` re-applies the idempotent shim on EVERY run. Confirm all four with the first two Verify commands; if any is missing, add it to the shim idempotently (`alter role … bypassrls`, a `pg_class.relrowsecurity` guard, plain re-runnable grants) and record the addition in HANDOFF. Only if the local database is beyond repair: `source scripts/db/_env.sh && super_psql -c "drop database churchapp"` then `bash scripts/db/local-up.sh` (`super_psql` works in every 1.2 path; `.local-pg/PG_SUPER_URL` exists only in some). CI starts fresh either way.
7. **`supabase/tests/helpers.sql`** — re-runnable (`create schema if not exists app_test`, `create or replace function`), header "test helpers — apply before `tests/rls/*.sql`; local and hosted SQL editor; never part of a migration". `grant usage on schema app_test to anon, authenticated, service_role` and `grant execute on all functions in schema app_test to anon, authenticated, service_role` at the end. Two families:
